statement: Any m x n complex matrix M can be factored into the singular value decomposition M = U Σ V*, where U is an m x m unitary matrix, Σ is an m x n rectangular diagonal matrix with non-negative real entries, and V is an n x n unitary matrix (with V* being its conjugate transpose).

symbols.meaning: Left unitary matrix whose columns are orthonormal eigenvectors of M M* (extended to an orthonormal basis)
Rectangular diagonal matrix containing singular values (non-negative square roots of eigenvalues of D) padded with zeros
Right unitary matrix whose columns are eigenvectors of M* M
Matrix whose columns are the orthonormal eigenvectors of M* M corresponding to non-zero eigenvalues
Matrix whose columns are orthonormal eigenvectors of M* M corresponding to zero eigenvalues
Diagonal matrix containing the strictly positive eigenvalues of M* M
Block diagonal matrix [D, 0; 0, 0] containing all eigenvalues of M* M
Matrix with orthonormal columns formed by normalized images M V_1 D^(-1/2)
Matrix whose columns complete the columns of U_1 to an orthonormal basis of C^m
Number of non-zero eigenvalues of M* M (rank of M)

steps.text: Because M* M is positive semi-definite and Hermitian, by the spectral theorem there exists an n x n unitary matrix V such that V* M* M V = D_bar = [D, 0; 0, 0], where D is an ℓ x ℓ diagonal and positive definite matrix of the non-zero eigenvalues of M* M, with ℓ <= min(n, m).

Partition V as V = [V_1, V_2], where the columns of V_1 (dimension n x ℓ) and V_2 (dimension n x (n - ℓ)) contain the eigenvectors of M* M corresponding to non-zero and zero eigenvalues, respectively. Then [V_1*; V_2*] M* M [V_1, V_2] = [V_1* M* M V_1, V_1* M* M V_2; V_2* M* M V_1, V_2* M* M V_2] = [D, 0; 0, 0], which implies V_1* M* M V_1 = D and V_2* M* M V_2 = 0, the latter implying M V_2 = 0. Unitary-ness of V gives V_1* V_1 = I_1, V_2* V_2 = I_2, and V_1 V_1* + V_2 V_2* = I_12.

Verify that the columns of U_1 are orthonormal: U_1* U_1 = D^(-1/2) V_1* M* M V_1 D^(-1/2) = D^(-1/2) D D^(-1/2) = I_1. Since the columns of U_1 are orthonormal in C^m, choose U_2 such that U = [U_1, U_2] forms an m x m unitary matrix extending U_1 to an orthonormal basis.

Define Σ = [[D^(1/2), 0; 0, 0]; 0] of dimension m x n, where zero rows are added or removed to match the number of columns of U_2. Multiplying gives U Σ V* = [U_1, U_2] Σ [V_1, V_2]* = [U_1, U_2] [D^(1/2) V_1*; 0] = U_1 D^(1/2) V_1* = M, yielding the factorization M = U Σ V*.

assumptions.assumption: M is an m x n matrix with finite dimensions over the real or complex field.
assumptions.breaks_when: M is an infinite-dimensional operator without appropriate compactness properties or defined over an incompatible scalar field.

assumptions.assumption: M* M is positive semi-definite and Hermitian, permitting spectral decomposition via a unitary matrix.
assumptions.breaks_when: The conjugate transpose / adjoint operation is not defined or the underlying vector space lacks a standard inner product.

failure_modes.signature: Singular matrix inversion error or division by zero.
failure_modes.cause: Attempting to include zero eigenvalues of M* M in the diagonal factor D rather than separating them into V_2 and restricting D to strictly positive eigenvalues.

failure_modes.signature: Dimension mismatch during matrix multiplication U Σ V*.
failure_modes.cause: Failing to pad or truncate zero blocks in Σ to match dimensions (m - ℓ) x (n - ℓ) so that Σ has overall dimensions m x n.
